definition: Nondescript means lacking any distinctive or interesting features; so plain and ordinary that nothing about it stands out.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word nondescript. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know nondescript should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The nondescript beige office building on the corner housed three separate law firms, yet most people who worked downtown couldn't have picked it out of a lineup.
Something plain simply has no special decoration or feature, though a plain thing can still be easy to describe; nondescript goes further — nothing about it registers at all.
Something unremarkable goes a step further than nondescript, giving observers nothing at all worth commenting on.

Generic stresses that something could be any one of many identical things — a generic hotel room looks like every other hotel room. Nondescript makes a different point: nothing about the thing itself can be described or remembered, whether or not copies of it exist.

Anonymous means carrying no name or identity — an anonymous donor, an anonymous office tower with no sign on it. Nondescript is about features, not names: a nondescript building offers nothing worth noticing. A striking landmark can still be anonymous if no one knows what it is.

Forgettable says a thing slips out of memory the moment you look away. Nondescript explains why: there was never a distinctive feature to hold onto. One word describes the effect on you; the other describes the thing itself.

After the merger, the company moved into a nondescript strip-mall unit between a dry cleaner and a phone-repair shop, choosing the anonymous location specifically so rival firms wouldn't notice how fast it was growing.
Nothing about the building's plain, generic exterior gave away the successful company operating inside — that forgettable blandness is exactly what "nondescript" describes.
Nondescript is a neutral, everyday word — not quite an insult, but it does suggest blandness.
It's most often used for buildings, vehicles, clothing, or appearances that blend into the background.
